changes.name: Fogport Cults
changes.entry:
Fogport has churches, clubs, lodges, unions, societies, supper rooms, neighborhood watches, philosophical drinking circles, and organizations that insist they are not cults because they keep minutes.

The following groups are useful as rumors, suspects, enemies, patrons, mistaken accusations, or street-level trouble. Some are magical. Some are criminal. Some are simply what happens when desperate people discover that ritual can make a bad situation worse in a more interesting direction.

Cults and Trouble Societies

The Candle-Eaten

Description: Poor families who believe candles can consume grief, guilt, and memory.

Activity: Burn written confessions inside fat candles made with hair, blood, or stolen funeral wax.

Where: Cellars beneath cheap chapels in Nine Spoons.

The Choir of Locked Teeth

Description: A polite singing cult obsessed with silencing unworthy mouths.

Activity: Kidnap loudmouths, gossips, informants, and inconvenient witnesses for muting rituals.

Where: An abandoned dental surgery near Blackwake.

The Fog-Bride Society

Description: Widows, jilted lovers, and lonely clerks ceremonially married to the fog.

Activity: Drown symbolic spouses, sometimes using real substitutes when the rite grows hungry.

Where: Tide stairs at dawn, especially in Lastlight.

The Sons of the Ninth Spoon

Description: Local toughs who claim Nine Spoons was chosen by hidden saints.

Activity: Extortion disguised as neighborhood protection and holy tax collection.

Where: The back room of a soup house with nine nailed spoons over the door.

The Bell Gutters

Description: Bellworks laborers who worship the sound inside broken machinery.

Activity: Feed teeth, coins, fingers, and secrets into dead condensers to wake them.

Where: Inside disused fog-factory intake pipes.

The Velvet Guillotine

Description: Former aristocrats who romanticize the executions after the Catastrophe.

Activity: Hold masked trials against modern officials and arrange theatrical murders.

Where: Private supper rooms near the Grand Promenade.

The Little Drowned School

Description: A child-led cult imitating lessons from dead teachers heard in rain barrels.

Activity: Steal books, chalk, bones, and occasionally teachers.

Where: A flooded schoolhouse in the Shambles.

The Salt Petitioners

Description: Desperate sailors who believe the sea can be sued in ritual court.

Activity: Stage legal hearings against storms, ships, drowned captains, and unpaid debts.

Where: Courthouse steps during fog-heavy nights.

The Order of the Kind Knife

Description: Surgical mystics who believe pain can be removed by giving it to someone else.

Activity: Perform illegal operations and pain-transference sacrifices.

Where: The rear room of a charity clinic.

The Ashen Bridesmen

Description: Men who dress as mourners for disasters that have not happened yet.

Activity: Sabotage weddings, launches, openings, and speeches to fulfill proper grief.

Where: A burned ballroom in Lastlight.

The Saints of Missing Doors

Description: Door-worshippers who believe every vanished doorway leads to a better Fogport.

Activity: Steal doors from homes, prisons, temples, and offices for alignment rituals.

Where: A lumber warehouse near Heliot Station.

The Crab Parliament

Description: Dockside eccentrics who interpret crab movement as civic law.

Activity: Release marked crabs into meetings, trials, gang disputes, and marriages.

Where: An under-pier market beside Blackwake.

The Red Thread Mercy

Description: Midwives and matchmakers who bind fate through blood-red thread.

Activity: Arrange marriages, pregnancies, betrayals, and accidental inheritances.

Where: Laundry yards, birthing rooms, and backstairs kitchens.

The Iron Nursery

Description: Thrallo sympathizers, labor organizers, and extremists obsessed with collars.

Activity: Steal collar fragments for rituals meant to birth giants of justice.

Where: Chain sheds near the harbor cranes.

The Smoke Accountants

Description: Bureaucrats who believe every sin must be entered into a divine ledger.

Activity: Blackmail citizens using ritual audits, impossible paperwork, and corrected lives.

Where: A basement archive beneath a tax office.

The Blind Lamplighters

Description: People who put out lamps so truer lights can be seen.

Activity: Extinguish whole streets before robberies, sacrifices, or disappearances.

Where: Lamp depots and dark tram stops.

The Feast Beneath

Description: Cannibal gourmands who claim eating the wicked improves public morals.

Activity: Host banquets where criminals, rivals, and informants become courses.

Where: A collapsed restaurant below the Grand Promenade.

The Moth Court

Description: Fashionable occultists who worship flame, beauty, and ruin.

Activity: Lure ambitious youths into glamour rituals that burn away identity.

Where: Costume salons and illegal theaters.

The Eel-Tongued

Description: Smugglers who believe eels carry messages from drowned gods.

Activity: Use eel guts for divination before crimes, betrayals, and harbor deals.

Where: Fish cellars beneath taverns.

The Society of the Second Face

Description: Mask-wearers who believe true personality lives beneath the skin.

Activity: Steal faces symbolically, socially, and sometimes literally.

Where: Grig mask workshops after closing.

The Clockless Minute

Description: Time fanatics who worship the instant the Catastrophe began.

Activity: Stop clocks, freeze victims in ritual poses, and repeat one minute endlessly.

Where: Clocktower maintenance rooms.

The Harbor Saints Militant

Description: Violent dock preachers who protect laborers and punish exploiters.

Activity: Beat foremen, rescue debtors, and demand blood offerings from bosses.

Where: Cargo chapels made from stacked transit crates.

The Pale Arithmetic

Description: Mathematicians and gamblers who think probability is a god with debts.

Activity: Sacrifice luck from one person to bless another.

Where: Illegal counting houses near Blackwake.

The Hushed Menagerie

Description: Wealthy monster collectors who want to restore the lost royal zoo.

Activity: Buy, breed, and release creatures to recreate proper wonder.

Where: Private gardens behind walled estates.

The Tomorrowless

Description: Catastrophe survivors who believe the future is vulgar and should be prevented.

Activity: Ruin apprenticeships, births, inventions, promotions, and fresh starts.

Where: A ruined nursery near the old palace sinkhole.
